out.window: The market runs from listing to July 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. The rules give no explicit start date; the most plausible reading is that ISW map status at any point up to the deadline counts. From the as_of date of July 18, about 13 days are left. out.qualifying_criteria: YES requires any part of the intersection at 48.494901N, 37.365342E in Toretske to be shaded red on the ISW map. Three shading types count: Assessed Russian Control, Assessed Russian Advance, or Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours. The shading must persist through the next ISW update. Russian control through a negotiated settlement also counts. Infiltration-only shading does not count, nor do claims, assaults, or Ukrainian or Russian reports of fighting 'near' Toretske.
out.evidence_vs_crowd: On July 14, 15 and 17, Ukraine's General Staff reported repeated Russian assaults 'in the area of' or 'toward' Toretske. So Russia is actively trying and is within striking distance, which supports a non-trivial probability. Other evidence points the other way. ISW said Russian forces made no confirmed advances in the Dobropillia tactical area on July 13–14. ISW also reported that Russia's overall gains in June 2026 averaged only about 1 km²/day, roughly 16 times slower than in June 2025. The front is grinding slowly, and ISW is conservative and often marks contested areas as infiltration rather than advance. Turning a contested settlement intersection red within 13 days is therefore unlikely. A negotiated settlement before July 31 is very unlikely. The crowd's 11.7% looks slightly high given the slow pace and the lack of confirmed advances, so I shade it down modestly.
